surface: The column dropdown menu of a right-to-left grid: opening it from the keyboard, End to the Alignment item, ArrowLeft into its submenu and ArrowRight back, as the direction swaps the keys, and Escape back to the grid.

steps.note: Shift+Alt+ArrowDown on B2 of the right-to-left grid opens its column's menu with the first item highlighted. Required: the item and the menu role. Finding: NVDA with Chromium reads the item and its position (`1 of 6`) without the word menu, as in grid-core; VoiceOver with Chromium says nothing when the menu opens, as in the dropdown-menu scenario, and nothing on any later step of this one. Finding (the grid's): the readers disagree on the item's position, as grid-core records: `1 of 6` with NVDA and Chromium, `1 of 2` with NVDA and Firefox, `1 of 11` with VoiceOver and WebKit. The items carry no `aria-posinset` or `aria-setsize`, so each browser counts them its own way.
End highlights the last item, Alignment, the parent of a submenu; NVDA and VoiceOver with WebKit say `Alignment, collapsed`.

In a right-to-left grid ArrowLeft opens the submenu, toward the side it opens on, with its first item, Left, highlighted; NVDA reads it. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit read only the parent item again, `Alignment expanded menu item`, in one run of two, as in the left-to-right context menu, and Left before the parent item in the other.

ArrowRight closes the submenu, and the focus returns to its parent item, Alignment, which NVDA and VoiceOver with WebKit say with its collapsed state. Finding: VoiceOver with Chromium says nothing (the open step).

Escape closes the menu and the focus returns to the grid. Opening the menu from the keyboard selects the whole column and clamps the focus cell to row 0, so the cell is B1; NVDA spells the reference apart (`B 1`), the synonym. NVDA and VoiceOver with WebKit say the cell. Finding: VoiceOver with Chromium says nothing (the open step).
